Fit Hidden Markov Models for Movement Data Classification

Source: R/fitHMM.wrap.R
fitHMM.wrap.Rd

Wrapper around momentuHMM to fit 2-state or 3-state Hidden Markov Models (HMM) to animal movement trajectories. Supports global, individual-level, or group-level model fitting.

Usage

fitHMM.wrap(
  data,
  ids = NULL,
  coordNames = c("x", "y"),
  coordtype = "UTM",
  mean.step.1 = NULL,
  sd.step.1 = NULL,
  mean.step.2 = NULL,
  sd.step.2 = NULL,
  ang.con.1 = NULL,
  ang.con.2 = NULL,
  stationary = FALSE,
  mode = "global",
  group.col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame containing spatial tracking trajectories.

ids

Character. Column name containing individual identifiers. Default is NULL.

coordNames

Character vector of length 2 specifying the X and Y coordinate column names. Default is c("x", "y").

coordtype

Character. Coordinate type passed to momentuHMM::prepData (e.g., "UTM" or "LL"). Default is "UTM".

mean.step.1

Numeric. Initial mean step length for state 1 (Transit).

sd.step.1

Numeric. Initial standard deviation of step length for state 1 (Transit).

mean.step.2

Numeric. Initial mean step length for state 2 (Encamped).

sd.step.2

Numeric. Initial standard deviation of step length for state 2 (Encamped).

ang.con.1

Numeric. Initial concentration parameter for turning angle in state 1 (Transit).

ang.con.2

Numeric. Initial concentration parameter for turning angle in state 2 (Encamped).

stationary

Logical. If TRUE, fits a 3-state model (including a stationary state) and re-maps state 3 to state 2 post-estimation. Default is FALSE.

mode

Character. Fitting mode: "individual" (one model per ID), "groups" (one model per defined group), or "global" (single model for all data). Default is "global".

group.col

Character. Column name identifying groups when mode = "groups". Default is NULL.

...

Additional arguments passed to fitHMM.

Value

An object of class disperseR containing:

data

A data.frame with movement parameters and Viterbi-decoded state assignments.

models

A list of fitted momentuHMM model objects.

Details

Step lengths are modeled using a gamma distribution and turning angles using a wrapped Cauchy distribution. In 2-state models, state 1 corresponds to Transit and state 2 to Encamped. Although the 2-state model generally performs well, in datasets lacking clear transit movements and containing abundant stationary periods, movement classification may be biased towards identifying stationary movements as Encamped and all other movements as Transit. In such cases, a 3-state model including a stationary state can improve state discrimination. The stationary state is initialized with a step-length prior equal to one tenth of the Encamped state (mean.step.2 ) prior from the 2-state model.

Examples

# \donttest{
trk <- sim_tracks[sim_tracks$ID == "F02", c("ID", "x", "y")]
hmm <- fitHMM.wrap(trk, ids = "ID",
                   mean.step.1 = 600, sd.step.1 = 400,
                   mean.step.2 = 80, sd.step.2 = 50,
                   ang.con.1 = 0.7, ang.con.2 = 0.1)
#> Fitting one model for all individuals.
#> =======================================================================
#> Fitting HMM with 2 states and 2 data streams
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------------
#>  step ~ gamma(mean=~1, sd=~1)
#>  angle ~ wrpcauchy(concentration=~1)
#> 
#>  Transition probability matrix formula: ~1
#> 
#>  Initial distribution formula: ~1
